mod5_amino_acids.proteins_diverse_versatile: p69: proteins are ubiquitous, diverse and versatile and mediate most cellular activities; linear polymers built from 20 amino acids (like letters of an alphabet); ball-and-stick, ribbon and space-filling models show the same protein
mod5_amino_acids.aa_four_groups_alpha_carbon: p69: four components bonded to the alpha carbon: amino group, carboxyl group, H, R group; the first three are identical in all amino acids
mod5_amino_acids.aa_charged_physiological_ph: p69: at physiological pH the amino group is NH3+ and the carboxyl group is COO-
mod5_amino_acids.r_group_determines_properties: p69: the R group (side chain) makes each amino acid unique and sets its chemical and physical properties
mod5_amino_acids.r_group_classification_criteria: p70: R groups classified by polarity (polar/nonpolar), interaction with water (hydrophilic/hydrophobic) and charge at physiological pH (acidic -, basic +, neutral)
mod5_amino_acids.hydrophobic_aa_buried_vdw: p70: hydrophobic (nonpolar) R groups tend to be buried in the protein interior, aggregating away from water; weak van der Waals forces between them add stability
mod5_amino_acids.hydrophilic_aa_hbond_surface: p70: polar R groups contain electronegative atoms (O, N) giving partial charges, so they H-bond with each other or water; hydrophilic amino acids usually sit on the outer surface
mod5_amino_acids.acidic_basic_charged_ionic: p70: basic R groups are positively charged and acidic R groups negatively charged at physiological pH; charged groups form ionic bonds with each other and with other charged molecules
mod5_amino_acids.glycine_flexibility: p71: glycine's R group is H, so its alpha carbon is not asymmetric; small and nonpolar, it allows free rotation about the C-N bond and makes the backbone flexible
mod5_amino_acids.proline_rigidity: p71: proline's R group bonds back to its amino group, restricting rotation about the C-N bond and limiting folding around proline
mod5_amino_acids.cysteine_disulfide: p71: cysteine's R group has a sulfhydryl (-SH); two cysteines form an S-S disulfide cross-bridge within one protein or between proteins
mod5_amino_acids.peptide_bond_dehydration: p71: a peptide bond joins the carboxyl group of one amino acid to the amino group of the next in a dehydration (condensation) reaction that releases H2O
mod5_amino_acids.n_terminus_c_terminus: p71: a polypeptide has a free amino group at its amino end (N-terminus) and a free carboxyl group at its carboxyl end (C-terminus); polypeptide is used synonymously with protein

mod5_protein_structure.sequence_determines_folding: p72: the order of amino acids (R groups) determines how a protein folds, and its structure determines its function
mod5_protein_structure.four_levels_conformation: p72: four levels of structure (1, 2, 3, 4); the protein's 3D conformation is described by 2, 3 and 4
mod5_protein_structure.primary_structure_sequence_n_to_c: p72: primary structure = linear amino-acid sequence written from amino (N) to carboxyl (C) end in 3- or 1-letter code; coded by the genome; determines 2, 3, 4 structure
mod5_protein_structure.r_groups_alternate_sides: p72: R groups alternate sides along the chain, which affects folding and R-group interactions
mod5_protein_structure.secondary_backbone_hbonds_only: p73: secondary structure = local conformation from H-bonds between backbone C=O and N-H groups of nearby amino acids; R groups are not involved; two types: alpha helix and beta sheet
mod5_protein_structure.alpha_helix_i_plus_4: p73: alpha helix is right-handed and very stable; the C=O of one amino acid H-bonds to the N-H of the amino acid four residues along
mod5_protein_structure.beta_sheet_parallel_antiparallel: p73: beta sheet = segments lying side by side in a pleated conformation, parallel or antiparallel, held by H-bonds between C=O of one strand and N-H of another strand of the same polypeptide
mod5_protein_structure.tertiary_r_group_interactions: p74: tertiary structure = 3D conformation of a whole single chain, set by the distribution of hydrophilic and hydrophobic R groups and bonds between R groups: H-bonds, hydrophobic interactions, ionic bonds, and covalent disulfide bonds
mod5_protein_structure.tertiary_functional_form_active_site: p74: tertiary structure is usually the functional form (unless the protein has subunits); the overall shape creates enzyme active sites and places exterior R groups that govern interactions with other molecules
mod5_protein_structure.quaternary_subunits_homo_hetero: p74: quaternary structure = arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits, held by the same bond types as tertiary; identical subunits = homodimer, non-identical = heterodimer

mod5_translation_machinery.central_dogma_translation_final: p75: transcription uses DNA as template to make mRNA; translation uses the mRNA base sequence to specify amino-acid order; translation is the final stage of the central dogma
mod5_translation_machinery.translation_components: p75: translation needs mRNA, ribosomes, tRNAs, aminoacyl tRNA synthetases, and initiation, elongation and release factors
mod5_translation_machinery.ribosome_rna_protein_subunits: p75: ribosomes are the site of translation; RNA + protein complexes of a small and a large subunit; eukaryotic ribosomes are larger than prokaryotic ones
mod5_translation_machinery.ribosome_a_p_e_sites: p76: three tRNA sites in the large subunit: A (aminoacyl-tRNA enters), P (holds the tRNA carrying the growing peptide), E (empty tRNA exits)
mod5_translation_machinery.ribosome_moves_5_to_3: p76: the mRNA runs through the ribosome between the subunits; the ribosome moves along the mRNA 5' to 3', reading codons
mod5_translation_machinery.codon_triplet_nonoverlapping: p76: a codon is three adjacent nucleotides specifying one amino acid; codons are read as a nonoverlapping series of triplets
mod5_translation_machinery.reading_frame: p76: the reading frame is set by where reading begins; shifting the starting point changes every downstream codon (ZWTHEBIGBOY example)
mod5_translation_machinery.trna_adapter_structure: p76: tRNAs are adapters of 70-90 nucleotides that base-pair with themselves into a cloverleaf; the amino acid attaches to the 3'-OH of the 5'-CCA-3' end; three anticodon bases sit in the anticodon loop
mod5_translation_machinery.aminoacyl_trna_synthetase_charging: p77: aminoacyl tRNA synthetases attach each specific amino acid to the 3' end of its specific tRNA (uncharged tRNA -> charged tRNA); each binds one tRNA and its amino acid; very accurate
mod5_translation_machinery.codon_anticodon_antiparallel: p78: the anticodon base-pairs with the codon antiparallel: the first (5') codon base pairs with the last (3') anticodon base
mod5_translation_machinery.genetic_code_64_redundant: p78: 64 codons specify 20 amino acids; many amino acids have more than one codon, so the code is redundant (degenerate); codons are read 5' to 3' with the standard code
mod5_translation_machinery.start_stop_codons: p78/p80: AUG is the start codon (methionine is the first amino acid); UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons

mod5_translation_process.translation_three_stages: p78: translation has three stages: initiation (AUG recognized, Met first), elongation (amino acids added one by one), termination (chain released)
mod5_translation_process.euk_initiation_cap_scanning: p79: in eukaryotes initiation factors bring the small subunit and Met-tRNA to the 5' cap; the complex scans to the first AUG; the large subunit then joins and the initiation factors are released
mod5_translation_process.elongation_steps_peptidyl_transferase: p79: an aminoacyl-tRNA enters the A site and pairs with the codon; the chain is transferred from the P-site tRNA to the A-site amino acid; peptide bond formation is catalyzed by the peptidyl transferase center of the large subunit, made of rRNA, between the A and P sites
mod5_translation_process.translocation_one_codon: p79: the ribosome then shifts one codon, moving the uncharged tRNA to the E site and the peptide-bearing tRNA to the P site and freeing the A site
mod5_translation_process.termination_release_factor: p80: at a stop codon (UAA, UAG, UGA) a protein release factor binds the A site; the bond linking the polypeptide to the tRNA breaks, completing the carboxyl terminus
mod5_translation_process.prok_initiation_shine_dalgarno: p80: prokaryotic mRNAs have no 5' cap; the ribosome binds internal Shine-Dalgarno sequences (5'-AGGAGGU-3') and starts at the first downstream AUG
mod5_translation_process.polycistronic_mrna: p80: one prokaryotic mRNA can code for several polypeptides (polycistronic); a eukaryotic mRNA is translated from the first AUG after the cap
mod5_translation_process.elongation_termination_conserved: p79-80: elongation and termination are similar in prokaryotes and eukaryotes; the differences are in initiation

mod5_regulation_sorting.gene_expression_regulation_levels: p81: not all genes are expressed all the time; regulation at DNA accessibility, transcription factors, RNA processing and post-translational modification
mod5_regulation_sorting.post_translational_modification: p81: many proteins are made inactive and activated by cleavage or modifications such as phosphorylation
mod5_regulation_sorting.translation_starts_cytosol: p81: translation begins on ribosomes in the cytosol; a protein's destination depends on its signal sequences
mod5_regulation_sorting.sorting_signals_destinations: p81: no signal -> stays in cytosol; amino-terminal signal -> mitochondria or chloroplasts; internal signal -> nucleus (free ribosomes)
mod5_regulation_sorting.srp_er_targeting: p82: an ER signal sequence at the amino end is bound by the signal recognition particle (SRP), which halts translation; SRP binds its receptor on the ER; the ribosome is passed to a channel, SRP leaves, translation resumes and the chain is threaded into the lumen; the signal sequence is cleaved
mod5_regulation_sorting.rough_er_protein_fates: p82: proteins made on the rough ER end up embedded in the ER membrane, in the lumen of the endomembrane system, or secreted
mod5_regulation_sorting.signal_anchor_membrane_protein: p82: a signal-anchor sequence stops threading; the channel releases the protein sideways into the membrane, where it stays as an integral membrane protein (N-terminus in the lumen in the figure)
mod5_regulation_sorting.gene_expression_overview_euk: p83: eukaryotic gene expression: transcription and RNA processing (cap, tail, splicing) in the nucleus; mRNA exits through nuclear pores; translation in the cytosol; noncoding RNAs (tRNA, rRNA) are also transcribed; many ribosomes can translate one mRNA; chains fold into proteins

mod6_energy_metabolism.cells_need_energy_work: p86: cells need a membrane, information molecules (nucleic acids, proteins) and energy for work: movement, growth, pumping ions, reactions
mod6_energy_metabolism.phototroph_vs_chemotroph: p86: phototrophs capture energy from sunlight (plants most common); chemotrophs obtain energy from chemical compounds (animals most common)
mod6_energy_metabolism.autotroph_vs_heterotroph: p86: autotrophs make organic carbon from CO2 (inorganic carbon); heterotrophs must obtain carbon from organic molecules made by other organisms
mod6_energy_metabolism.metabolic_classification_examples: p86: photoautotrophs (plants, cyanobacteria), photoheterotrophs (heliobacteria, most green nonsulfur bacteria), chemoautotrophs (sulfur-oxidizing, hydrogen bacteria), chemoheterotrophs (most bacteria, animals)
mod6_energy_metabolism.metabolism_definition_pathways: p87: metabolism = all chemical processes in an organism that maintain life; continuous; linked so that products of one reaction are reactants of the next (metabolic pathways)
mod6_energy_metabolism.anabolism_vs_catabolism: p87: anabolism builds macromolecules from smaller units and requires energy (ATP); catabolism breaks molecules into smaller units and releases energy (makes ATP)
mod6_energy_metabolism.potential_vs_kinetic_energy: p87: potential energy is stored energy (position/structure); kinetic energy is energy of motion; one form can convert to the other
mod6_energy_metabolism.chemical_energy_bond_strength: p88: chemical energy is potential energy held in bonds; strong bonds = less potential energy, weak bonds = more potential energy

mod6_atp.atp_energy_currency: p88: cells store energy in a readily accessible chemical form; ATP is the most common energy currency, used by all cells
mod6_atp.atp_structure_adp_amp: p88: ATP = adenine + ribose + three phosphate groups; ADP has two phosphates, AMP one; adenine + ribose = adenosine
mod6_atp.atp_cellular_work_examples: p88: ATP powers cellular work: DNA, RNA and protein synthesis, vesicle movement, pumping substances across membranes, and steps of breaking down fats, proteins and sugars
mod6_atp.atp_phosphate_bonds_energy: p88: ATP's chemical energy is held in the bonds connecting its phosphate groups; these bonds are weak (high potential energy), and breaking them releases energy for work
mod6_atp.atp_hydrolysis_exergonic_repulsion: p91: ATP + H2O -> ADP + Pi is exergonic (-7.3 kcal/mol); at physiological pH the phosphate groups are negatively charged and repel one another; ADP has lower potential energy

mod6_thermodynamics.first_law_conservation: p89: first law: energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another; total energy before = total energy after
mod6_thermodynamics.second_law_direction_entropy: p89: second law: events proceed from higher to lower energy states; such events are thermodynamically favourable (spontaneous, no external energy input); every transformation loses usable energy (often as heat), increasing entropy, so no conversion is 100% efficient
mod6_thermodynamics.electrons_drop_release_energy: p89: when electrons move from a higher to a lower energy level, energy is released as heat or light
mod6_thermodynamics.chemical_reaction_bonds_change: p90: in a chemical reaction atoms keep their identity but the bonds linking them change (CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3)
mod6_thermodynamics.concentration_direction_reversible: p90: the relative concentrations of reactants and products influence whether a reaction proceeds forward or backward
mod6_thermodynamics.gibbs_free_energy_delta_g: p90: Gibbs free energy (G) is the energy available to do work; delta G = G(products) - G(reactants) (final - initial)
mod6_thermodynamics.exergonic_vs_endergonic: p90: products with more G than reactants: +delta G, endergonic, thermodynamically unfavourable (nonspontaneous), needs energy input; reactants with more G: -delta G, exergonic, favourable (spontaneous), releases energy
mod6_thermodynamics.delta_g_enthalpy_entropy: p91: total energy H = G + energy lost to entropy, so delta G = delta H - T delta S (T in kelvin; temperature increases molecular motion and disorder)

mod6_coupling.positive_delta_g_concentrations: p92: cells run +delta G reactions by keeping reactant-to-product ratios above the equilibrium ratio (supplying reactants, removing products)
mod6_coupling.energetic_coupling_atp: p92: coupling an endergonic reaction to an exergonic one (usually ATP hydrolysis) makes the net delta G negative; the reactions share an intermediate (Pi); glucose + ATP -> glucose-6-phosphate + ADP: +3.3 and -7.3 give -4.0 kcal/mol

mod6_enzymes.activation_energy_transition_state: p91: every reaction needs an input of activation energy (EA) to break bonds and reach the transition state; reactants must have enough kinetic energy to clear the barrier
mod6_enzymes.enzyme_lowers_ea_not_delta_g: p91: enzymes speed reactions by lowering EA; delta G is the same with and without the enzyme
mod6_enzymes.enzymes_are_proteins_active_site: p92: enzymes are proteins; the active site is formed by specific amino acids, often far apart in the sequence, brought together by folding
mod6_enzymes.active_site_binds_stabilizes_ts: p92: the active site binds the substrate(s), stabilizes the transition state (lowering EA) and converts substrate to product
mod6_enzymes.lock_key_vs_induced_fit: p93: lock-and-key model (substrate fits a rigid site) vs induced fit (the enzyme changes shape as substrate binds)
mod6_enzymes.enzyme_catalysis_anabolic_catabolic: p93: E + S <-> ES <-> EP <-> E + P; enzymes catalyze both catabolic (splitting) and anabolic (joining) reactions and are released unchanged
mod6_enzymes.inhibitors_reversible_irreversible: p93: enzyme activity can be reduced by reversible and irreversible inhibitors and increased by activators
mod6_enzymes.competitive_vs_noncompetitive: p93: a competitive inhibitor binds the active site and competes with the substrate; a noncompetitive inhibitor binds elsewhere and changes the enzyme's shape
mod6_enzymes.feedback_inhibition_allosteric: p93: in feedback inhibition the end product of a pathway inhibits an enzyme early in the pathway (e.g. isoleucine inhibits threonine dehydratase, an allosteric enzyme); keeps balance and conserves energy

bridge_links_m1to4.m1_ribosome_non_ems: Module 1: ribosomes are non-membrane (non-EMS) structures, free in the cytosol or bound to the ER
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_prok_euk_differences: Module 1: prokaryotes lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotes compartmentalize
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_cell_property_energy: Module 1: cell properties include acquiring and using energy and carrying out metabolism
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_kingdom_nutrition: Module 1: plants are autotrophs; fungi and animals are heterotrophs; protists vary
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_model_organisms_ecoli: Module 1: E. coli and other model organisms used to study molecular processes
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_bond_strengths: Module 2: covalent bonds are strongest; ionic bonds, hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions are weaker but act together
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_electronegativity_polarity: Module 2: electronegativity differences make polar bonds with partial charges
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_hydrophobic_effect_water: Module 2: water's hydrogen bonding excludes nonpolar molecules, driving hydrophobic clustering
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_ph_ionization_groups: Module 2: pH sets the ionization of carboxyl and amino groups
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_condensation_hydrolysis: Module 2: condensation builds polymers and releases water; hydrolysis splits them using water
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_macromolecule_monomers: Module 2: the four macromolecule classes and their monomers
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_nucleotide_atp_scaffold: Module 2: nucleotides (base + sugar + phosphate); ATP shares the nucleotide scaffold
bridge_links_m1to4.m2_functional_groups: Module 2: functional groups (hydroxyl, carboxyl, amino, sulfhydryl, phosphate) and their chemistry
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_endomembrane_secretory_route: Module 3: rough ER -> Golgi -> vesicles -> plasma membrane, lysosomes or secretion
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_membrane_protein_types: Module 3: integral vs peripheral proteins; membrane-spanning segments are hydrophobic
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_lumen_topology: Module 3: the lumen side of ER/Golgi membranes becomes the outside face of the plasma membrane after vesicle fusion
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_mito_chloro_semi_autonomous: Module 3: mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA and bacteria-like ribosomes but import most proteins; endosymbiotic origin
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_nuclear_pores_transport: Module 3: nuclear pores let small molecules pass freely and actively transport large ones
bridge_links_m1to4.m3_active_transport_atp: Module 3: primary active transport (pumps) uses ATP to move solutes against gradients
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_template_coding_strands: Module 4: the template strand is read 3'->5'; the mRNA matches the nontemplate (coding) strand with U for T
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_mrna_processing_cap_tail_splicing: Module 4: eukaryotic pre-mRNA receives a 5' cap, a poly(A) tail and splicing
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_coupled_transcription_translation: Module 4: in prokaryotes translation begins while transcription is still under way
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_central_dogma_flow: Module 4: DNA -> RNA -> protein; transcription vs translation
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_rna_types: Module 4: mRNA, tRNA and rRNA are all transcribed from DNA
bridge_links_m1to4.m4_ntp_energy_polymerization: Module 4: incoming nucleoside triphosphates supply the energy for each phosphodiester bond (pyrophosphate released)
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_virus_not_cell: Module 1: viruses have genes but no ribosomes or metabolism, so they can reproduce only inside host cells
bridge_links_m1to4.m1_cell_structure_function: Module 1: a cell's structures (nucleus, ribosomes, organelles) determine what it can do
